title: Glintt's product-led healthtech model, not its stack, is what rules it out
content:
Glintt is recorded as an Iberian healthtech leader through Glintt Life, running its own healthtech products. The screen's judgement is that it is product-led, and that is the disqualifier — not the vertical, which is a good one, and not the platform, since there is no third-party platform to complement.

The product-led exclusion works the same way here as elsewhere in the workbook: a firm that ships its own software has an internal roadmap that any new record layer competes with, and a revenue model that does not depend on assembling other people's components. Partnering asks it to route feature demand outward instead of into its own backlog.

One caveat on the record itself: the figures held for Glintt are twelve years old, dating from 2014. Anything size- or growth-dependent in this assessment is therefore unreliable, and the only durable part of the verdict is the model — product-led — which is a structural property unlikely to have reversed.
